model_annotation: The plot shows the development of exports and imports (both as lines on the left scale) together with a balance (“Saldo”) shown as vertical bars on a right-hand scale, all in “Mrd. US-Dollar.” The x-axis is a time axis labeled with years from 2020 through 2023 (linear scale), with major year labels and many evenly spaced minor ticks between them. The left y-axis is labeled in billions of US dollars and runs from 0 to 400 with evenly spaced tick marks every 50. A right y-axis is also present for the balance bars, ranging from −200 to 400 with tick marks every 100. The import series is a solid blue line with no markers; it starts near 200 in 2020, dips to roughly 165 early in 2020, then rises through 2021 into the mid‑200s, reaches around 285–290 in early 2022, declines to about 255–265 around 2022–2023, and then increases again toward the end of 2023 to roughly 340–350. The export series is a solid purple line with no markers; it begins around 135 in 2020, drops to about 90 early in 2020, then climbs through 2021 to around 140–150, rises further into early 2022 to roughly 175–180, eases down to about 160–170 during 2022–2023, and ends near 180 by late 2023. The balance (“Saldo”) is shown as light-blue vertical bars referenced to the right axis; the bars are mostly below zero across the period, generally around roughly −50 to −100 for much of 2020–2022, and become more negative toward late 2023, reaching approximately −150 to −170 at the end.
